title: Call prototype serializer and friendly error translations
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: We need a standardized on-wire representation (prototype serializer) for function/tool call schemas and a mapping layer that converts low-level validator failures into concise, actionable user-facing error messages. This ticket covers: (1) a recommended JSON schema envelope and compact authoring conventions for function parameters, (2) runtime validation behavior (strict vs tolerant modes), and (3) an error translation table + telemetry hooks for common validation failures. Goal: reduce ambiguous tool-invocation failures and cut developer troubleshooting time by ~50% for schema-related errors.
background: Customers and internal SDKs repeatedly run into unclear function-call failures when models generate near-valid JSON. Existing validator output is too verbose (full schema diffs) and not actionable. We also need a compact authoring format so model authors can write parameter contracts without large vanilla JSON Schema blobs. Prior art: lightweight envelopes used by similar platforms, plus our internal diagnostics patterns.
design_decisions: Introduce a compact 'proto' envelope that sits one level above JSON Schema to support short-hand types, required lists, and common constraints (min/max, enum).
Support two server-side validation modes: 'strict' (reject on first mismatch) and 'repair' (attempt coercions/field repairs then return diagnostics).
Surface errors with a single canonical 'user_message', a short 'code', and an optional 'repair_hint' string. Do NOT return raw schema diffs to clients by default.
Emit structured telemetry events for validation failures with tags: model_variant, route, validation_code, repair_attempted (true/false).
validation_modes: strict: immediate rejection with single, primary error (useful for production routes with guaranteed contract adherence)
repair: attempt deterministic repairs (string->number coercion, missing defaults) and attach diagnostics; return repaired payload plus warnings
error_translation_table: invalid_type -> code: VALIDATION_INVALID_TYPE; user_message: 'Field "{field}" expected a {expected} but got {actual}.', repair_hint: 'Try sending the value as {expected} (e.g., remove quotes for numbers).', telemetry_tag: 'invalid_type'

missing_required -> code: VALIDATION_MISSING_REQUIRED; user_message: 'Missing required field "{field}".', repair_hint: 'Include "{field}" in your function call payload. If "{field}" is optional for your upstream flow, mark it as optional in the proto.', telemetry_tag: 'missing_required'
enum_mismatch -> code: VALIDATION_ENUM_MISMATCH; user_message: '"{field}" must be one of {allowed}.', repair_hint: 'Use one of the allowed values: {allowed}.', telemetry_tag: 'enum_mismatch'

string_too_long -> code: VALIDATION_TOO_LONG; user_message: 'Value for "{field}" is too long (max {max}).', repair_hint: 'Truncate to {max} characters or migrate to a different parameter.', telemetry_tag: 'too_long'
telemetry_spec: Emit event 'validation.failure' with properties: code, field, route, model_variant, client_id (if available), repair_attempted (true/false). Events should be sampled at 10% for high-throughput routes by default.
runtime_behavior_notes: When repair mode is enabled, runtime applies deterministic coercions in the following priority: null->default, string-numeric coercion, enum case-normalization, boolean string normalization. If multiple repairs are applied, include a top-level 'repairs' list in diagnostics. In strict mode, return an HTTP 422 with a single translated error object.
acceptance_criteria: Define and land the proto->JSON Schema converter in runtime with tests for the shorthand features.
Implement validator that runs in both strict and repair modes and exposes the error translation mapping.
SDKs (JS + Python) can opt-in to receive 'repair' responses and surface repair_hints in developer consoles.
Telemetry events emitted for validation failures are wired to existing observability dashboards and have dashboards configurable by route/model.
Documentation page with authoring examples, validation mode guidance, and a migration guide for existing tool schemas.
tasks: spec: write proto envelope spec and converter (ENG-642910-TSPEC)
sdk: expose validation mode toggle and repair payload handling (ENG-642910-SDK-JS, ENG-642910-SDK-PY)
telemetry: add validation.failure event and dashboard tiles (ENG-642910-TEL)
docs: author 'Function schemas and friendly errors' guide and quickstart (ENG-642910-DOCS)
qa: fuzz test model outputs and assert human-readable errors for common failure classes (ENG-642910-QA)
risks: Over-eager repairs could mask upstream modeling failures and lead to silent correctness regressions.
Returning too much repair detail might leak PII if not redacted; ensure redaction pipeline runs before user_message is surfaced.
Telemetry volume spike if we naively emit events for every validation failure on busy routes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal opt-in): land proto spec + converter, enable repair mode behind flag for internal teams (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (beta): add SDK toggles, publish docs, enable telemetry, invite 3 pilot customers (3 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): default to strict for hosted public routes, allow repair opt-in per-route and per-customer (scheduled with release runtime-2.4).
qa_criteria: Unit tests for proto->jsonschema conversion with 98% coverage of shorthand features.
End-to-end tests where model-generated near-miss JSON triggers repair path and returns repaired payload plus diagnostics.
Manual UX review of error messages in Console and SDK, confirming concise wording and no raw schema dumps.
open_questions: What should be the retention period for validation.failure events in telemetry? Default 30 days or align with existing error retention?
Should repair mode be allowed for enterprise private deployments by default, or require an explicit opt-in during onboarding?
Do we want to ship an automatic client-side linter in the SDKs that surfaces proto authoring issues pre-deployment?
comments: 2026-02-12: PM review (Jonas Patel) - asked to include migration guide for existing JSON Schema-heavy tool contracts.
2026-02-18: Design review (Maya Chen) - suggested short examples for common patterns (strings, enums, nested objects) and recommended a single-line error message limit of 120 chars.
2026-02-27: Engineering sync - decided repair mode will only apply deterministic coercions; fuzzy repairs (e.g., fuzzy enum match) deferred to future epic.
2026-03-05: Telemetry (Ravi Shah) - agreed to 10% sampling on high-throughput routes and add a toggle for full-emit during pilot.

2026-03-12: Implementation update (Diego Morales) - proto->schema converter prototype complete; basic translations wired; starting SDK integration next sprint. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2214
notes: Keep error messages short and prescriptive. If a translation requires exposing the input value for clarity, ensure it's redacted for PII-sensitive fields before returning to callers. Follow existing Redaction guidelines in security playbook.
